name: Feature Selection Benchmark for Tabular Deep Learning
description: Academic tabular benchmarks often contain small sets of curated features. In contrast, data scientists typically collect as many features as possible into their datasets, and even engineer new features from existing ones. To prevent overfitting in subsequent downstream modeling, practitioners commonly use automated feature selection methods that identify a reduced subset of informative features. Existing benchmarks for tabular feature selection consider classical downstream models, toy synthetic datasets, or do not evaluate feature selectors on the basis of downstream performance. Motivated by the increasing popularity of tabular deep learning, we construct a challenging feature selection benchmark evaluated on downstream neural networks including transformers, using real datasets and multiple methods for generating extraneous features. evaluation_method: downstream performance (e.g. accuracy/MSE) and feature-selection quality
reputation: A specialized research benchmark with limited broad community adoption, mainly used in tabular deep learning and feature selection research.
notes: Benchmark focuses on surrogate feature selection for tabular deep learning; results depend on downstream model and synthetic/extraneous feature generation; not a standard single-metric benchmark.
